To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrated a quantum measurement of the degree polarization (DOP) for a light beam in the presence of rapid fluctuations of its polarization state.
we have demonstrated a coherent quantum measurement of the degree polarization for the case of polarization state fluctuations.
a quantum measurement for the DOP of a light beam has been developed and demonstrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
quantum information and communication, quantum cryptography, quantum metrology, quantum imaging, quantum computing and quantum sensing.
the development of quantum optical methods to characterize the degree of polarization.
the development and application of new techniques for the generation, detection, and manipulation of quantum states of light.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polarization state of a light field can be measured with a quantum efficiency of up to 90%, which is a significant improvement over the classical measurement.
quantum measurements of the degree of polarizations of a light beam is a very important tool in the field of quantum optics.
the quantum measurement method is not only a theoretical possibility, but a practical and efficient method for the determination of polarization properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum measurement of the degree is a good alternative for the determination of DOP in the case of a light beam whose polarization state is fluctuating fast.
we demonstrate that the degree of polarization can be measured with a precision of better than 0.1%, using only 1.4×10^5 photons per measurement.

we have developed a new technique for measuring the degree of polarization, which is based on the quantum theory of measurement, and which can be applied in a wide range of situations, such as for measuring the DOP of a laser beam, for measuring the DCPM of a laser beam and for measuring the DPC of a laser beam.
The main takeaway from our work is that

quantum measurement can be used to determine the degree of polarization with high precision, even for light beams whose polarization state fluctuates rapidly in time, and for which the polarimetric technique cannot be applied.
the DOP measurement is not limited by the photon number but by the photon indistinguishability.
a quantum measurement can be used to determine the DOP of light with a precision better than that achievable with the classical polarimetric measurement.
